In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful.

Surah ash-Shura. His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Ha Mim﴾ ﴿Ayn Sin Qaf﴾ ﴿Thus does He reveal to you, and to those before you, Allah, the Mighty, the Wise﴾.

We have already presented the discussion of the disjointed letters (al-huruf al-muqatta'a) at the beginning of Surah Hud.

As for az-Zamakhshari's explanation of this verse, ﴿Thus does He reveal to you﴾, meaning: like that revelation, or like that Book, He reveals to you and to the Messengers before you, Allah.

That is, what this surah contains of meanings, Allah has revealed to you the like of it in other surahs, and revealed it to His Messengers before you, in the sense that Allah the Exalted repeated these meanings in the Qur'an and in all the heavenly Books, because of the eloquent admonition and the great kindness they contain for His servants among the first and the last. End of his words.

The apparent meaning of his words is that the comparison in His saying ﴿Thus does He reveal﴾ relates to the one revealed (the object, in the form of the passive participle).

The more evident view is that the comparison concerns the verbal noun meaning, which is the revealing (al-iha').

As for His saying in this noble verse, ﴿and to those before you﴾, He does not here explicitly name any of those before him to whom He revealed, as He revealed to him. However, He has named a group of them in Surah an-Nisa', and He stated there that some of them He did not relate their account to him, and that He revealed to them and sent them to cut off the arguments of creation in the life of this world. This is in His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, We have revealed to you as We revealed to Noah and the prophets after him, and We revealed to Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, the Tribes, Jesus, Job, Jonah, Aaron, and Solomon, and We gave David the Psalms﴾ ﴿And messengers We have related their stories to you before, and messengers We have not related their stories to you; and Allah spoke directly to Moses﴾ ﴿Messengers as bringers of good tidings and warners, so that mankind will have no argument against Allah after the messengers. And ever is Allah Exalted in Might and Wise﴾ (p-٣٨)[an-Nisa': 163–165].

As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Allah, the Mighty, the Wise﴾, He, exalted and high is He, praised Himself therein by His name the Mighty and His name the Wise, after mentioning His sending down His revelation to His prophets, as He said in the aforementioned Surah an-Nisa': ﴿And ever is Allah Mighty and Wise﴾, after mentioning His revelation to His Messengers.

We have already presented at the beginning of Surah az-Zumar that inductive study of the Qur'an shows that Allah, exalted and high is He, when He mentions the sending down of His Book, follows that with some of His beautiful names and sublime attributes, and we mentioned many examples of that.

Most of the seven readers, except Ibn Kathir, recited this letter as (yuhi) with a kasra on the ha', in the active voice. On the reading of the majority, His saying (Allah, the Mighty, the Wise) is the subject (fa'il) of yuhi.

Ibn Kathir recited it (yuha ilayka) with a fatha on the ha', in the passive voice. On this reading, His saying (Allah, the Mighty, the Wise) is the subject of a deleted verb whose estimated form is yuha, as we have already explained in Surah an-Nur in the discussion of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿He is glorified therein morning and evening by men﴾ [an-Nur: 36–37].

We have already presented the meanings of revelation (al-wahy) together with the Arabic evidences in Surah an-Nahl, in the discussion of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And your Lord inspired to the bee﴾ [an-Nahl: 68], and in other places.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 42, verse 4:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And He is the Most High, the Most Great﴾.

In this noble verse He, may He be glorified and exalted, describes Himself with highness (al-'uluw) and greatness (al-'azamah), and these are among the comprehensive attributes (al-sifat al-jami'ah), as we have previously discussed in surah al-A'raf, in the commentary on His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then He established Himself upon the Throne﴾ [al-A'raf: 54].

What this noble verse includes of His describing Himself with these two comprehensive attributes, which encompass every perfection and majesty, has come in the like of it in other verses, such as:

• His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And its preservation does not tire Him, and He is the Most High, the Most Great﴾ [al-Baqarah: 255].

• His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever Most High, Most Great﴾ [al-Nisa': 34].

• His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, the Great, the Exalted﴾ [al-Ra'd: 9].

• His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And to Him belongs the majesty in the heavens and the earth﴾ and the verse [al-Jathiyah: 37].

And beyond that from the verses.

[p-39] His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿The heavens are almost splitting apart from above them, and the angels exalt their Lord with praise and ask forgiveness for those on the earth﴾.

Most of the Seven Readers (al-Sab'a, the seven canonical reciters), except Nafi' and al-Kisa'i, read ﴿takādu﴾ (تَكادُ) with a feminine ta at the start, because the heavens (al-samawat) are feminine. Nafi' and al-Kisa'i read ﴿yakādu﴾ (يَكادُ) with a masculine ya, because the feminization of "the heavens" is not real (ghayr haqiqi).

Most of the Seven, except Abu 'Amr and Shu'ba from 'Asim, read ﴿yatafaṭṭarna﴾ (يَتَفَطَّرْنَ) with a ta after the ya, a fatha on the ta, and a fatha on the shaddated ta', as the imperfect of tafaṭṭara, meaning "split open."

Abu 'Amr and Shu'ba from 'Asim read ﴿yanfaṭirna﴾ (يَنْفَطِرْنَ) with a sakin nun after the ya and a kasra on the lightened ta', as the imperfect of infaṭarat, like His saying: ﴿When the sky breaks apart﴾ [al-Infitar: 1], meaning "split open."

As for His saying ﴿takādu﴾, it is the imperfect of kāda, which is a verb of approximation (fi'l muqarabah). It is known that it governs the subject and predicate. Its meaning as a verb of approximation is that it indicates that the subject is close to being characterized by the predicate.

So the meaning of the verse, according to the first reading, is that the heavens came close to being characterized by splitting, and according to the second reading, by being torn apart.

Know that the reason the heavens came close to splitting in this noble verse is something on which the scholars have two views, and each is supported by a Qur'anic text.

The first view: the meaning is that the heavens almost split because of fear of God, awe and reverence. This view is supported by His saying before it: ﴿And He is the Most High, the Mighty﴾ [al-Shura: 4], because His exaltedness and greatness caused the heavens that fear, awe and reverence, until they almost split.

On this view, His saying after it, ﴿and the angels exalt their Lord with praise and ask forgiveness for those on the earth﴾, is clearly related to what precedes it, because the meaning is that the heavens are in extreme fear of Him, may He be exalted, and awe and reverence toward Him. Likewise their inhabitants among the angels: they ﴿exalt their Lord with praise﴾, that is, they declare Him free of everything unfitting to His perfection and majesty, while affirming for Him every perfection and majesty, out of fear of Him, awe and reverence, as He said, may He be exalted: ﴿And the thunder exalts [God] with His praise, and [so do] the angels out of fear of Him﴾ [al-Ra'd: 13]. And He said, may He be exalted: ﴿And to Allah prostrate whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth of creatures, and the angels, and they are not arrogant. They fear their Lord above them and do what they are commanded﴾ [al-Nahl: 49–50].

[p-40] Thus, because of the intensity of their fear of God and their reverence for Him, they exalt their Lord with praise, and they fear for the people of the earth. Therefore they ask forgiveness for them, out of fear for them of the wrath and punishment of God. This view is supported by His saying: ﴿Indeed, We offered the trust to the heavens and the earth…﴾ up to His saying: ﴿and they declined to bear it and feared it﴾ [al-Ahzab: 72], because ishfaq means fear.

His saying in this noble verse, ﴿and ask forgiveness for those on the earth﴾, means specifically those among them who believed, repented to God and followed His path, as He clarified by His saying: ﴿Those who carry the Throne and those around it exalt their Lord with praise and believe in Him and ask forgiveness for those who believed﴾ [Ghafir: 7].

So His saying ﴿for those who believed﴾ clarifies the intended meaning of His saying ﴿for those on the earth﴾. What further clarifies this is His saying about them, that they say in their request for forgiveness for the believers: ﴿Forgive those who repent and follow Your way﴾ [Ghafir: 7], because that clearly indicates that they do not ask forgiveness for the disbelievers.

The second view: the meaning is that the heavens almost split because of the immensity of the slander which the disbelievers invented against the Creator of the heavens and the earth, may He be majestic and exalted, namely that He took a son, exalted be He far above that, high indeed. This view is clarified in Surah Maryam in His saying: ﴿And they say, "The Most Merciful has taken a son." Certainly you have done an atrocious thing. The heavens almost split from it, the earth splits open, and the mountains collapse in ruin, that they attribute to the Most Merciful a son. And it is not appropriate for the Most Merciful to take a son. There is none in the heavens and earth but that he comes to the Most Merciful as a servant﴾ [Maryam: 88–93], as we have already explained.

The most that can be said about this view is that this verse of al-Shura contains a general statement about the cause of the splitting of the heavens, and that was clarified in the aforementioned verse of Maryam. Both views are true.

His saying in this noble verse, ﴿splitting from above them﴾, has several views among the scholars.

It was said: ﴿yatafaṭṭarna﴾ refers to the heavens, and ﴿from above them﴾ refers to the earths, but the distance of this view is obvious, as you see.

[p-41] Some said: ﴿from above them﴾ means that every heaven splits above the one next to it.

Al-Zamakhshari said in al-Kashshaf: If you say, "Why did He say, 'from above them'?" I say: because the greatest of the signs and the most indicative of majesty and greatness are above the heavens, namely the Throne, the Footstool, and the rows of angels resounding with glorification and sanctification around the Throne, and what none knows the reality of except Allah, the Exalted, of the traces of His great dominion. Therefore He said, "splitting from above them," that is, the splitting begins from their upper direction.

Or, because the word of disbelief came from those under the heavens, so the expected phrasing would have been "splitting from below them, from the direction from which the word came." But this was exaggerated: it was made to have an effect in the upward direction, as if it were said: "they almost split from the direction above them, let alone the direction below them."

A parallel to this in exaggeration is His saying, may He be glorified and exalted: ﴿Boiling water will be poured over their heads﴾ [al-Hajj: 19], ﴿by which whatever is in their bellies will be melted﴾ [al-Hajj: 20], so He made the boiling water affect their inner parts. End of quotation, the point of the purpose from it.

This applies only on the view that the cause of the aforementioned splitting is their slander against God in their saying: ﴿"The Most Merciful has taken a son"﴾ [Maryam: 88].

We have already mentioned above that Surah Maryam indicates this. On this view, the connection of His saying "and the angels exalt their Lord with praise" to what precedes it is that the disbelievers, though they utter the greatest and most abominable disbelief, the angels are the opposite of them, since they constantly remember God and obey Him.

This is clarified by His saying: ﴿But if they are arrogant, those who are near your Lord exalt Him by night and by day, and they never tire﴾ [Fussilat: 38], and His saying: ﴿If these disbelieve in it, We have already entrusted it to a people who are not disbelievers in it﴾ [al-An'am: 89], as we have already explained at the end of Surah Fussilat.

* *

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Unquestionably, Allah is the Forgiving, the Merciful﴾.

In this noble verse, He, may He be majestic and exalted, affirmed that He is the Forgiving, the Merciful, and He made clear in it that He alone is specifically characterized by this.

[p-42] These two matters contained in this noble verse have been clarified in other places.

As for His being specifically the one, may He be majestic and exalted, who forgives sins, He mentioned it in His saying: ﴿And who forgives sins except Allah?﴾ [Al 'Imran: 135]. The meaning is: none forgives sins except Allah. In the hadith: "My Lord, I have wronged myself greatly, and none forgives sins except You," the hadith [continues]. And in the hadith of the Master of Seeking Forgiveness: "O Allah, You are my Lord, there is no god but You, You created me," the hadith [continues], and in it: "and I acknowledge my sin, so forgive me, for none forgives sins except You."

The way this verse indicates that Allah alone is the one who forgives sins is that the pronoun of separation (ḍamīr al-faṣl), between the predicate and the subject in His saying ﴿Unquestionably, Allah is the Forgiving, the Merciful﴾, indicates this, as is known in its proper place.

As for the second matter, namely His emphasizing that He is the Forgiving, the Merciful, He emphasized it here with the opening particle (ḥarf al-istiftah), which is "alā," and the particle of emphasis, which is "inna." He clarified this in many verses:

• such as His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah forgives all sins. Indeed, it is He who is the Forgiving, the Merciful﴾ [al-Zumar: 53].

• And His saying: ﴿And indeed, I am forgiving toward one who repents and believes﴾ [Ta-Ha: 82], the verse.

• And His saying: ﴿Indeed, your Lord has vast forgiveness﴾ [al-Najm: 32].

• And His saying about the disbelievers: ﴿Say to those who disbelieve: if they cease, they will be forgiven what has already passed﴾ [al-Anfal: 38].

• And His saying about those who said that Allah is the third of three: ﴿Will they not repent to Allah and seek His forgiveness? And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 74].

Verses of this kind are many.

So we ask Allah, may He be majestic and exalted, the Generous, the Kind, the Forgiving, the Merciful, to forgive us all our sins, to pass over all our misdeeds, to admit us into His Garden despite what we have done, and to forgive our Muslim brothers. Indeed, He is Forgiving and Merciful.

**Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 42, verse 6:**

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And those who take protectors other than Him—Allah is Watcher over them, and you are not a guardian over them.﴾

His saying, may He be exalted, in this noble verse: ﴿They have taken protectors besides Him﴾. That is, they associated with Him partners whom they worship besides Him, as He made clear in His saying: ﴿And those who take protectors besides Him say, "We only worship them so that they may bring us nearer to Allah in position. Indeed, Allah will judge between them concerning that over which they differ. Indeed, Allah does not guide one who is a liar.﴾ [Az-Zumar: 3]. (p-43)

• And His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And those who disbelieve—their protectors are the taghut. They bring them out of the light into darknesses. Those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally.﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 257].

• And His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, they have taken the devils as protectors besides Allah, and they think that they are guided.﴾ [Al-A'raf: 30].

• And His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿That is only the Shaytan, who frightens you of his supporters﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 175]. That is, he frightens you of his supporters.

• And His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So fight against the supporters of Shaytan﴾, and the verse [An-Nisa': 76].

Allah, may He be exalted, has rebuked them for taking Shaytan and his offspring as protectors besides Him, in His saying: ﴿Then do you take him and his descendants as protectors besides Me, while they are an enemy to you? Wretched is the exchange for the wrongdoers.﴾

He, may He be exalted and sublime, has commanded the following of this Great Qur'an and has forbidden the following of the protectors taken besides Him, at the beginning of Surah Al-A'raf, in His saying: ﴿Follow what has been sent down to you from your Lord and do not follow other than Him as protectors. Little do you remember.﴾ [Al-A'raf: 3].

From the verses mentioned, you have come to know that the protectors of the disbelievers whom they took and worshipped besides Allah are of two kinds. The first of them is the devils. The meaning of their worship of Shaytan is their obedience to him in what he makes attractive to them of disbelief and sins. Thus their association with him is an association of obedience (shirk al-ta'ah). The verses that indicate their worship of the devils in the sense mentioned are many, such as:

• His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Did I not charge you, O children of Adam, that you not worship Shaytan?﴾, and the verse [Ya-Sin: 60].

• And His saying, may He be exalted, concerning Ibrahim: ﴿O my father, do not worship Shaytan﴾, and the verse [Maryam: 44].

• And His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿They invoke besides Him only female deities, and they invoke none but a rebellious Shaytan﴾ [An-Nisa': 117]. That is, they worship none but a rebellious Shaytan.

• And His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿They will say, "Exalted are You; You are our protector, not them. Rather, they used to worship the jinn; most of them were believers in them.﴾ [Saba': 41].

• And His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿His authority is only over those who take him as an ally and those who associate others with Him.﴾ [An-Nahl: 100].

• And His saying: ﴿And indeed, the devils inspire their allies to dispute with you. And if you obey them, indeed you would be associators [of others with Allah].﴾ [Al-An'am: 121].

And other verses besides these.

The second kind is the idols, as Allah explained by His saying: ﴿We only worship them so that they may bring us nearer to Allah in position﴾, and the verse [Az-Zumar: 3].

As for His saying, may He be exalted, in this noble verse: ﴿Allah is Watcher over them﴾, that is, He is Observer over them, Guardian over them of everything they do of disbelief and sins. And at its beginning is their taking protectors whom they worship besides Allah.

In the verse there is a great threat to every associator.

And His saying, may He be exalted, in this noble verse: ﴿And you are not a guardian over them﴾.

That is: you are not, O Muhammad, one appointed over them to guide whom you wish to guide from among them. Rather, you are only a warner, and you have conveyed the message and given counsel.

The one appointed over them is Allah, who guides whom He wills from among them and misguides whom He wills, as He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿You are only a warner, and Allah is over all things Disposer of affairs.﴾ [Hud: 12]. And He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And if your Lord had willed, those on earth would have believed—all of them entirely. Then, would you compel the people until they become believers? And it is not for a soul to believe except by permission of Allah, and He places defilement upon those who do not reason.﴾ [Yunus: 99–100]. And He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And if their turning away has been difficult for you, then if you are able to seek a tunnel into the earth or a ladder into the sky to bring them a sign—[you may do so]. And if Allah had willed, He would have gathered them upon guidance, so do not be among the ignorant.﴾ [Al-An'am: 35]. The verses similar to these are many.

From what we have mentioned, you know that the correct verification regarding His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And you are not a guardian over them﴾, and what is similar to it of verses, is that it is not abrogated (mansukh) by the verse of the sword (ayat al-sayf). And Allah knows best.

**Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on Surah 42, verse 7:**

Allah's words: ﴿And thus We have revealed to you an Arabic Qur'an﴾.

We have already presented the verses that clarify this in Surah "al-Shu'ara'" in the discussion of His words: ﴿That you may be of the warners, in a clear Arabic tongue﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 194-195]. And in Surah "al-Mu'min" in the discussion of His words: ﴿An Arabic Qur'an, without any crookedness﴾ [al-Zumar: 28]. And in other places.

* *

Allah's words: ﴿That you may warn the Mother of Cities and those around it﴾.

In this noble verse, Allah, blessed and exalted, specified His Messenger's (ﷺ) warning to the Mother of Cities and those around it. The Mother of Cities is Makkah, may Allah protect it.

However, He made clear in other verses that his warning is general to both humankind and jinn (al-thaqalan), as in His words: ﴿Say, "O mankind, indeed I am the Messenger of Allah to you all"﴾ [al-A'raf: 158]. And His words: ﴿Blessed is He who sent down the Criterion upon His servant that he may be a warner to the worlds﴾ [al-Furqan: 1]. And His words: ﴿And We have not sent you except comprehensively to mankind﴾ [Saba': 28]. As we have explained this repeatedly in this blessed book.

We have already mentioned the answer concerning the specification of the Mother of Cities and those around it here, and in Surah "al-An'am" in His words: ﴿And that you may warn the Mother of Cities and those around it, and those who believe in the Hereafter believe in it﴾ [al-An'am: 92]. In our book "Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab" we said there: The answer is from two aspects.

The first: The intended meaning of His words ﴿and those around it﴾ includes the entire earth, as reported by Ibn Jarir and others, from Ibn 'Abbas.

The second aspect: Even if we concede, for the sake of argument, that His words ﴿and those around it﴾ cover only those near Makkah, may Allah protect it, such as the Arabian Peninsula for example, the other verses explicitly state generality, such as His words ﴿to be a warner to the worlds﴾ [al-Furqan: 1]. Mentioning some individuals of a general ('amm) term by way of its ruling does not specify it (takhsis) according to the majority of scholars. Only Abu Thawr disagreed with this.

We have already presented this clearly with its evidences in Surah "al-Ma'idah". So the verse according to this view is like His words ﴿And warn your closest kindred﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 214]; for it does not indicate the non-warning of others, as is clear. And Allah knows best. End of his quotation.

* *

Allah's words: ﴿And warn of the Day of Assembly, about which there is no doubt﴾ [al-Shura: 7].

This noble verse contains two matters. The first: among the rulings of His revealing this Arabic Qur'an to Our Prophet (ﷺ) is the warning of the Day of Assembly. His words ﴿and warn of the Day of Assembly﴾ are coordinated (ma'tuf) upon His words ﴿That you may warn the Mother of Cities﴾, meaning: in order that you may warn the Mother of Cities and that you may warn of the Day of Assembly. So one of the two objects is omitted in the first and one of them is omitted in the second. What was stated in each of them is evidence for what was omitted in the other. In the first, the second object is omitted, and the implied meaning is "That you may warn the Mother of Cities," i.e., the people of Makkah, "and those around it," of a severe punishment if they do not believe. In the second, the first object is omitted, i.e., and warn the people of the Day of Assembly, which is the Day of Resurrection, i.e., frighten them of what it contains of terrors and horrors, so that they may prepare for it in the abode of this world.

The second: the Day of Assembly mentioned is "about which there is no doubt," i.e., there is no doubt about its occurrence.

These two matters contained in this noble verse have come clarified in other verses.

As for his frightening people about the Day of Resurrection, it has been mentioned in several places in the Book of Allah,

• such as His words: ﴿And fear a Day when you will be returned to Allah﴾ [al-Baqarah: 281], and the rest of the verse.

• And His words: ﴿And warn them of the Approaching Day﴾ [Ghafir: 18], and the rest of the verse.

• And His words: ﴿Then how will you protect yourselves, if you disbelieve, from a Day that will make children grey-haired? The sky will be split by it﴾ [al-Muzzammil: 17-18].

• And His words: ﴿Do they not think that they will be resurrected for a tremendous Day, the Day when mankind will stand before the Lord of the worlds?﴾ [al-Mutaffifin: 4-6].

Verses similar to this are many.

As for the second of the two, namely that the Day of Resurrection is "about which there is no doubt," it has come in other places,

• such as His words: ﴿Allah – there is no deity except Him – will surely gather you on the Day of Resurrection, about which there is no doubt﴾ [al-Nisa': 87].

• And His words: ﴿So how will it be when We gather them for a Day about which there is no doubt?﴾ [Al 'Imran: 25].

• And His words: ﴿And that the Hour is coming, there is no doubt about it﴾ [al-Hajj: 7], and the rest of the verse.

• And His words: ﴿And when it was said, "Indeed the promise of Allah is true, and the Hour – there is no doubt about it," you said, "We do not know what the Hour is"﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 32], and the rest of the verse.

To other verses besides these.

The Day of Resurrection was only named the Day of Assembly because Allah gathers in it all of creation. The verses clarifying this meaning are many,

• such as His words: ﴿Say, "Indeed, the former and the latter will surely be gathered for the appointed time of a known Day"﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 49-50].

• And His words: ﴿This is the Day of Judgment; We have gathered you and the former peoples﴾ [al-Mursalat: 38].

• And His words: ﴿Allah – there is no deity except Him – will surely gather you on the Day of Resurrection﴾ [al-Nisa': 87], and the rest of the verse.

• And His words: ﴿The Day He will gather you for the Day of Assembly – that is the Day of mutual loss and gain﴾ [al-Taghabun: 9].

• And His words: ﴿That is a Day for which mankind will be gathered, and that is a Day of witnessing﴾ [Hud: 103].

• And His words: ﴿So how will it be when We gather them for a Day about which there is no doubt, and every soul will be paid in full what it earned, and they will not be wronged?﴾ [Al 'Imran: 25].

• And His words: ﴿And We gathered them, and We left none of them behind﴾ [al-Kahf: 47].

Allah has also explained the comprehensiveness of that gathering to include all animals and birds in His words: ﴿And there is no creature on the earth or bird that flies with its wings except that they are communities like you. We have not neglected in the Book anything. Then to their Lord they will be gathered﴾ [al-An'am: 38]. The verses indicating the aforementioned gathering are many.

* *

Allah's words: ﴿A party will be in Paradise and a party in the Blaze﴾.

What this noble verse indicates, that Allah created the creation and made from them a party who are fortunate, namely the people of Paradise, and a party who are wretched, namely the companions of the Blaze, has come clarified in other verses, such as His words: ﴿He is the One who created you; among you is a disbeliever and among you is a believer﴾ [al-Taghabun: 2]. And His words: ﴿And they will continue to differ, except those upon whom your Lord has mercy. And for that He created them﴾ [Hud: 118-119], i.e., for that difference between believer and disbeliever, wretched and fortunate, He created them — according to the correct view. The revealed texts indicating this are very many.

We have mentioned in our book "Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab" the way of reconciling His words ﴿And for that He created them﴾ [Hud: 119], according to the aforementioned interpretation, with His words ﴿And I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 56]. We will mention that, if Allah wills, in Surah "al-Dhariyat".

We have already presented the meaning of al-Sa'ir (the Blaze) with its Arabic evidences at the beginning of Surah "al-Hajj", in the discussion of His words: ﴿And he guides him to the punishment of the Blaze﴾ [al-Hajj: 4], and the rest of the verse. And al-Jannah (Paradise), in the language of the Arabs, is an orchard.

From this is the statement of Zuhayr ibn Abi Sulma:

"As if my two eyes, at the western well of a camel-drawn bucket, were watering a distant garden."

His words "jannatan suhqan" mean an orchard of tall palm trees. In the technical terminology of the Shari'ah, it is the abode of honour that Allah prepared for His friends on the Day of Resurrection.

Al-Fariq (a party) is a group of people, and it may be multiplied to more than two. From this is the statement of Nusayb: "The party of the people said, 'No,' and their party said, 'Yes,' and a party said, 'Woe to you, we do not know.'"

The justification for beginning with an indefinite noun in His words ﴿A party in Paradise﴾ is that it occurs in a context of detailed explanation.

A parallel to this from the speech of the Arabs is the statement of Imru' al-Qays:

"So when I drew near to her and began to weave, I forgot one garment and wove another."

[p. 48]

The words of His, exalted is He: ﴿And whatever you differ about, its judgment is with God.﴾

What this noble verse indicates, that whatever people differ about in rulings, its judgment belongs to God alone and not to anyone else, has been clarified in many verses.

Associating others with God in His judgment is like associating others with Him in worship. He said regarding His judgment: ﴿And He does not make anyone share in His judgment﴾ [al-Kahf: 26]. In the reading of Ibn 'Amir among the Seven, it is recited as ﴿وَلا تُشْرِكْ فِي حُكْمِهِ أَحَدًا﴾ (wa-la tushrik fi hukmihi ahadan, "and do not make anyone share in His judgment") in the prohibitive form (ṣīghat al-nahy), with the verb in the jussive after the prohibitive particle *lā*.

He said regarding associating others with Him in worship: ﴿So whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord, let him do righteous deeds and not associate anyone in the worship of his Lord﴾ [al-Kahf: 110]. The two matters are equal, as you see in their clarification, God willing.

From this you know that the lawful is what God has made lawful, the unlawful is what God has made unlawful, and the religion is what God has legislated. Therefore every legislation from other than Him is void, and acting upon it in place of God's legislation, for one who believes it is equal to it or better than it, is manifest disbelief (kufr bawāḥ) about which there is no dispute.

The Qur'an has indicated in many verses that there is no judgment for other than God, and that following the legislation of others is disbelief in Him. Among the verses indicating that judgment belongs to God alone is His saying: ﴿Judgment belongs only to God; He has commanded that you worship none but Him﴾ [Yūsuf: 40]. And His saying: ﴿Judgment belongs only to God; upon Him I have relied﴾ [Yūsuf: 67], and the verse continues. And His saying: ﴿Judgment belongs only to God; He relates the truth, and He is the best of deciders﴾ [al-An'ām: 57]. And His saying: ﴿And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed, those are the disbelievers﴾ [al-Mā'idah: 44]. And His saying: ﴿And He does not make anyone share in His judgment﴾ [al-Kahf: 26]. And His saying: ﴿Everything will perish except His face; to Him belongs the judgment, and to Him you will be returned﴾ [al-Qaṣaṣ: 88]. And His saying: ﴿To Him belongs praise in the first and the last, and to Him belongs the judgment, and to Him you will be returned﴾ [al-Qaṣaṣ: 70]. The verses of this kind are many.

We have already presented their clarification in Surah "al-Kahf" in the discussion of His saying: ﴿And He does not make anyone share in His judgment﴾ [al-Kahf: 26].

As for the verses indicating that following the legislation of other than God, as mentioned, is disbelief, they are very many, such as:

• His saying: ﴿His authority is only over those who take him as a guardian and those who associate others with Him﴾ [al-Naḥl: 100].
• His saying: ﴿And if you obey them, indeed you would be associators﴾ [al-Naḥl: 121].
• His saying: ﴿Did I not charge you, O children of Adam, that you not worship Satan﴾, and the verse continues [Yā-Sīn: 60].

The verses of this kind are very many indeed, as has preceded in its clarification in "al-Kahf."

[p. 49]

**Issue**

Know that God, Majestic and Exalted, has clarified in many verses the attributes of the one who deserves to have judgment belong to him. So every intelligent person should reflect on the attributes mentioned, which we will now clarify, God willing, and compare them with the attributes of human beings who legislate man-made laws (al-qawānīn al-waḍʿiyyah), and see whether the attributes of the one who holds legislation apply to them. Glory be to God, and exalted is He above that.

If they applied to them, which they will not, then let them follow their legislation.

But if it becomes certain that they are more base, more lowly, more humiliated, and smaller than that, then let them be kept to their limit, and let them not be raised by them to the station of lordship (rubūbiyyah), glory be to Him and exalted above having a partner in His worship, His judgment, or His dominion.

Among the Qur'anic verses by which God clarified the attributes of the one who holds judgment and legislation is His saying here: ﴿And whatever you differ about, its judgment is with God﴾, then He said, clarifying the attributes of the one who holds judgment: ﴿That is God, my Lord; upon Him I have relied, and to Him I turn in repentance﴾ ﴿Originator of the heavens and the earth; He made for you from yourselves mates, and among the cattle mates; He multiplies you thereby. There is nothing like Him, and He is the Hearing, the Seeing﴾ ﴿To Him belong the keys of the heavens and the earth; He extends provision to whom He wills and restricts it; indeed He is Knowing of all things﴾ [al-Shūrā: 10–12].

So is there among the disbelieving, corrupt legislators of satanic systems anyone who deserves to be described as the Lord to whom affairs are entrusted and upon whom one relies, and that He is the Originator (fāṭir) of the heavens and the earth — that is, their Creator and Inventor — without a prior pattern; and that He is the One who created for mankind mates, and created for them the eight mates of livestock mentioned in His saying: ﴿Eight mates: of sheep two﴾, and the verse continues [al-An'ām: 143]; and that there is nothing like Him, and He is the Hearing, the Seeing; and that to Him belong the keys of the heavens and the earth; and that He is the One who extends provision and restricts it — that is, narrows it upon whom He wills — and He is Knowing of all things?

So you, O Muslims, must understand the attributes of the one who deserves to legislate, to make lawful and unlawful, and do not accept legislation from a base, lowly, ignorant disbeliever.

The parallel of this noble verse is His saying: ﴿And if you dispute over anything, refer it to God and the Messenger, if you are believers in God and the Last Day. That is best and most favorable in outcome﴾ [al-Nisā': 59]. So His saying in it, ﴿refer it to God﴾, is like His saying in this one: ﴿its judgment is with God﴾.

[p. 50]

And after His saying ﴿refer it to God﴾, His Prophet (ﷺ) was astonished at those who claim faith while they want to take their disputes to one who does not possess the attributes of the one who holds judgment, the one referred to in the verse as the *ṭāghūt* (idol or any object of worship or obedience beyond God). Every litigation toward other than God's law is litigation toward the *ṭāghūt*. This is in His saying: ﴿Have you not seen those who claim they believe in what has been revealed to you and what was revealed before you, yet they desire to take their disputes to the ṭāghūt, although they were commanded to reject it? And Satan wants to lead them far astray﴾ [al-Nisā': 60].

So disbelief in the ṭāghūt, which God has stated He commanded them to do in this verse, is a condition of faith, as He clarified in His saying: ﴿Whoever disbelieves in the ṭāghūt and believes in God has grasped the most trustworthy handhold﴾ [al-Baqarah: 256].

From this it is understood that whoever does not disbelieve in the ṭāghūt has not held fast to the most trustworthy handhold, and whoever does not hold fast to it is among those who are ruined along with the perishing.

Among the verses indicating this is His saying: ﴿To Him belongs the unseen of the heavens and the earth; how clear is His sight and His hearing! They have no protector other than Him, and He does not make anyone share in His judgment﴾ [al-Kahf: 26].

So is there among the disbelieving, corrupt legislators anyone who deserves to be described as having the unseen of the heavens and the earth? And that his hearing and sight are emphasized because his hearing encompasses all audible things and his sight all visible things? And that there is no protector for anyone other than him?

Glory be to Him and exalted above that with great exaltedness.

Among the verses indicating this is His saying: ﴿And do not invoke with God another god; there is no god but He. Everything will perish except His face. To Him belongs the judgment, and to Him you will be returned﴾ [al-Qaṣaṣ: 88].

So is there among the disbelieving, corrupt legislators anyone who deserves to be described as the one God, and that everything will perish except His face, and that creation will return to him?

Blessed is our Lord, and exalted and sanctified is He, above having His attributes ascribed to the basest of His creation.

Among the verses indicating this is His saying: ﴿That is because when God alone is invoked, you disbelieve; but if others are associated with Him, you believe. So judgment belongs to God, the Most High, the Great﴾ [Ghāfir: 12].

[p. 51]

So is there among the disbelieving, corrupt legislators of satanic systems anyone who deserves to be described, in the greatest of heavenly books, as "the Most High, the Great"?

Glory be to You, our Lord, and exalted are You above all that is unbefitting Your perfection and majesty.

Among the verses indicating this is His saying: ﴿And He is God; there is no god but Him. To Him belongs praise in the first and the last, and to Him belongs the judgment, and to Him you will be returned﴾ ﴿Say: Have you considered, if God made the night perpetual over you until the Day of Resurrection, who is a deity other than God who could bring you light? Then will you not hear?﴾ ﴿Say: Have you considered, if God made the day perpetual over you until the Day of Resurrection, who is a deity other than God who could bring you a night in which you rest? Then will you not see?﴾ ﴿And from His mercy He made for you the night and the day, that you may rest therein and seek of His bounty, and perhaps you will be grateful﴾ [al-Qaṣaṣ: 70–73].

So is there among the makers of man-made laws anyone who deserves to be described as having praise in the first and the last, and that He is the One who turns the night and the day, thereby showing the perfection of His power and the greatness of His favor upon His creation?

Glory be to the Creator of the heavens and the earth, Majestic and Exalted, above having a partner in His judgment, His worship, or His dominion.

Among the verses indicating this is His saying: ﴿Judgment belongs only to God. He has commanded that you worship none but Him. That is the upright religion, but most of the people do not know﴾ [Yūsuf: 40].

So is there among those anyone who deserves to be described as the God worshipped alone, and that worshipping Him alone is the upright religion?

Glory be to God, and exalted is He above what the wrongdoers say, with great exaltedness.

Among them is His saying: ﴿Judgment belongs only to God; upon Him I have relied, and upon Him let those who rely [on Him] rely﴾ [Yūsuf: 67].

So is there among them anyone who deserves to be relied upon, and to whom affairs are entrusted?

Among them is His saying: ﴿And that you judge between them by what God has revealed, and do not follow their desires, and beware of them lest they tempt you away from some of what God has revealed to you. And if they turn away, then know that God intends only to afflict them for some of their sins, and indeed, many of the people are defiantly disobedient﴾ ﴿Do they then desire the judgment of jāhiliyyah (the age of ignorance)? And who is better than God in judgment for a people who are certain?﴾ [al-Mā'idah: 49–50].

So is there among those legislators anyone who deserves to be described as having a judgment that is by what God has revealed, and that it is opposed to following desires? And that whoever turns away from him, God afflicts him for some of his sins — because sins are not all punished except in the Hereafter? And that there is no judgment better than his for a people who are certain?

Glory be to our Lord, and exalted is He above all that is unbefitting His perfection and majesty.

Among them is His saying: ﴿Judgment belongs only to God; He relates the truth, and He is the best of deciders﴾ [al-An'ām: 57].

So is there among them anyone who deserves to be described as one who relates the truth, and that he is the best of deciders?

Among them is His saying: ﴿Shall I seek a judge other than God, while it is He who has revealed to you the Book, detailed? And those to whom We gave the Book know that it is sent down from your Lord in truth, so do not be among the doubters﴾ ﴿And the word of your Lord has been fulfilled in truth and justice﴾, and the verse continues [al-An'ām: 114–115].

So is there among those mentioned anyone who deserves to be described as the One who sent down this Book detailed, whose truth the People of the Book bear witness to, that it is sent down from your Lord in truth, and that His words have been fulfilled in truth and justice — that is, truthful in reports and just in rulings — and that there is no changer of His words, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing?

Glory be to our Lord; how great He is, and how exalted is His station!

Among them is His saying: ﴿Say: Have you considered what God has sent down to you of provision, and you made of it lawful and unlawful? Say: Did God permit you, or do you invent against God?﴾ [Yūnus: 59].

So is there among those mentioned anyone who deserves to be described as the One who sends down provision to creatures, and that there can be no making lawful or unlawful except by His permission? Because it is necessarily true that whoever created provision and sent it down is the one who has the right of disposal over it by making lawful and unlawful?

Glory be to Him, Majestic and Exalted, above having a partner in making lawful and unlawful.

Among them is His saying: ﴿And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed, those are the disbelievers﴾ [al-Mā'idah: 44].

[p. 53]

So is there among them anyone who deserves to be described by that?

Glory be to our Lord, and exalted is He above that.

Among them is His saying: ﴿And do not say, concerning what your tongues describe as falsehood, "This is lawful and this is unlawful," to fabricate against God falsehood. Indeed, those who fabricate against God falsehood will not succeed﴾ ﴿A brief enjoyment, and for them is a painful punishment﴾ [al-Naḥl: 116–117].

This passage shows that those who legislate other than what Allah has legislated only utter falsehood with their tongues, in order to fabricate it against Allah. It also shows that they will not prosper, that they will be given brief enjoyment and then subjected to a painful punishment. This is clear from how far their attributes are from the attributes of the One who has the right to make lawful and unlawful.

Among the proofs is His saying, ﴿Say: "Bring your witnesses who testify that Allah has forbidden this." If they testify, do not testify along with them.﴾ [al-An'am: 150]

His saying, ﴿Bring your witnesses,﴾ is a form of challenge (ta'jiz). They are unable to show the basis for the prohibition. This is clear evidence that no one other than Allah possesses the attributes of making lawful or unlawful. Since legislation and all rulings, whether legislative (shar'iyyah) or cosmic and predestined (kawniyyah qadariyyah), belong to the specific attributes of Lordship (rububiyyah), as the aforementioned verses indicate, whoever follows a legislation other than the legislation of Allah has taken that legislator as a lord and has associated him with Allah.

The verses indicating this are many. We have mentioned them repeatedly, and we will repeat those that are sufficient. Among them, and one of the clearest and most explicit, is that during the time of the Prophet (ﷺ) a debate took place between the party of the Most Merciful and the party of Satan concerning a ruling from the rulings of prohibition and permission. The party of the Most Merciful followed the legislation of the Most Merciful in His revelation regarding its prohibition, while the party of Satan followed the revelation of Satan regarding its permission.

Allah judged between them and gave a verdict concerning what they disputed, a heavenly, Qur'anic verdict recited in Surat "al-An'am."

The matter was that Satan, when he inspired his allies, said to them in his revelation: "Ask Muhammad about the sheep that dies. Who killed it?" They answered them that Allah was the one who killed it.

They said: "Then carrion is the slaughter of Allah. How do you say that what Allah slaughtered is forbidden? Yet you say that what you slaughter with your own hands is permitted. Therefore you are better than Allah and have a more lawful slaughter."

So Allah revealed, by the consensus (ijma') of those among the scholars whose view is considered, His saying: ﴿And do not eat of that over which the name of Allah has not been mentioned﴾ [al-An'am: 121], meaning carrion, that is, even if the disbelievers claim that Allah slaughtered it with His noble hand using a knife of gold. ﴿And indeed it is defiance﴾ [al-An'am: 121]. The pronoun refers to the eating understood from His saying "do not eat." His saying "defiance" means departure from obedience to Allah and following the legislation of Satan. ﴿And indeed the devils inspire their allies to dispute with you﴾ [al-An'am: 121], that is, by their saying: "What you slaughter is lawful, and what Allah slaughters is unlawful. Therefore you are better than Allah and have a more lawful slaughter." Then He clarified the heavenly verdict from the Lord of the worlds in judging between the two parties in His saying: ﴿And if you obey them, indeed you would be polytheists﴾ [al-An'am: 121]. This is a heavenly verdict from the Creator, exalted is He, in which He declared explicitly that whoever follows the legislation of Satan, which opposes the legislation of the Most Merciful, is a polytheist in relation to Allah.

This noble verse has been cited by some grammarians as an example of the omission of the lam preceding the oath (al-lam al-muwatti'ah lil-qasam). The evidence for the omitted lam is the absence of the particle fa' with the clause ﴿indeed you would be polytheists﴾. For if it were a conditional (shart), a preceding oath would not have been stated, and it would have been said: "fa-innakum lamushrikun" (then indeed you are polytheists), in accordance with his statement in the Khulasah (the summary of Ibn Malik's Alfiyyah):

﻿واقرنْ بفا حتمًا جوابًا لو جُعِل ... شرطًا لأنْ أو غيرِها لم يَنْجَعِل

"Conjoin with fa' necessarily the response, if it is made a condition with 'in' or other than it, it does not take effect."

This is the view of Sibawayh, and it is the correct one. Omitting the fa' in such a case is a poetic necessity (darurat al-shi'r).

As for what some claimed, that it is permissible absolutely, and that two verses of the Book of Allah indicate this: the first is His saying: ﴿And if you obey them, indeed you would be polytheists﴾.

The second is His saying: ﴿And whatever disaster strikes you is by what your hands have earned﴾ [42], with the omission of the fa' in the reading of Nafi' and Ibn Amir among the seven readers, which goes against verification (tahqiq).

Rather, the justification for omitting the fa' in the verse ﴿indeed you would be polytheists﴾ is the assumed omitted oath preceding the condition, indicated by the omission of the fa', in accordance with his statement in the Khulasah:

﻿واحذفْ لدى اجتماعِ شرطٍ وقسمْ ... جوابَ ما أَخَّرْتَ فهو مُلتزَمْ

"When a condition and an oath come together, omit the response of whichever you placed later; it is obligatory [to omit]."

Accordingly, the clause ﴿indeed you would be polytheists﴾ is the response of the assumed oath, and the response of the condition is omitted. So there is no evidence in the verse for the omission of the fa' mentioned.

As for its justification in the verse ﴿whatever disaster strikes you is by what your hands have earned﴾: in the reading of Nafi' and Ibn Amir, "ma" is a relative pronoun (mawsulah), as a number of the verifying scholars have affirmed. That is, "and that which strikes you of disaster is occurring and happening because of what your hands have earned."

As for the reading of the majority, "ma" is also a relative pronoun, and the entry of fa' into the predicate of the relative pronoun is permissible, just as its absence is permissible. Thus both readings follow a permissible matter.

An example of the entry of fa' into the predicate of the relative pronoun is His saying: ﴿Those who spend their wealth by night and by day, secretly and publicly, will have their reward with their Lord, and no fear will be upon them, nor will they grieve﴾ [al-Baqarah: 274]. This is common in the Qur'an.

Some said that "ma" in the reading of the majority is conditional (shartiyyah), and accordingly the joining of the response with fa' is obligatory.

As for the reading of Nafi' and Ibn Amir, it is a relative pronoun and nothing else, as is the verified view, if Allah wills.

That "ma" is conditional in one reading and relative in another presents no difficulty, because, as we have mentioned, the two readings in one verse are like two verses.

Among the verses that indicate something similar to what the verse of "al-An'am" mentioned indicates is His saying: ﴿His authority is only over those who take him as an ally and those who associate others with Him﴾ [al-Nahl: 100]. He explicitly stated their allegiance to Satan, that is, by following what adorns for them of disbelief and sins, in opposition to what the messengers brought. Then He explicitly stated that this is association with Him, in His saying: ﴿and those who associate others with Him﴾. He also explicitly stated that obedience in that which Satan legislates for them and adorns is worship of Satan.

It is well known that whoever worships Satan has associated others with the Most Merciful. He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Did I not charge you, O children of Adam, that you not worship Satan? Indeed, he is to you a clear enemy. And that you worship Me; this is a straight path. And he had already led astray from among you much of a generation. Did you not then use reason?﴾ [Ya-Sin: 60–62]. Among those who follow Satan's system are included, by way of entering in as allies, those who are included.

Then He clarified the final destination of whoever worshipped Satan in the worldly life, in His saying: ﴿This is Hell which you were promised. Burn therein today for what you used to deny. Today We seal over their mouths, and their hands speak to Us, and their feet testify to what they used to earn﴾ [Ya-Sin: 63–65]. He, exalted is He, said concerning His prophet Ibrahim: ﴿O my father, do not worship Satan. Indeed Satan has been to the Most Merciful a disobedient one﴾ [Maryam: 44]. His saying "do not worship Satan" means by following what he legislates of disbelief and sins, in opposition to what Allah has legislated.

He, exalted is He, said: ﴿They invoke besides Him only females, and they invoke only a rebellious devil﴾ [al-Nisa': 117]. His saying "and they invoke only a devil" means they worship only a rebellious devil.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And [mention] the Day He will gather them all and say to the angels, "Did these people used to worship you?" They will say, "Exalted are You; You are our protector, not them. Rather, they used to worship the jinn; most of them were believers in them."﴾ [Saba': 40–41].

His saying: ﴿Rather, they used to worship the jinn﴾ means they followed the devils and obeyed them in what they legislated and adorned for them of disbelief and sins, according to the more correct of the two interpretations.

Satan knows that their obedience to him, as mentioned, is association with him, as he himself declared and disowned them in the Hereafter, as Allah stated in Surat "Ibrahim" in His saying: ﴿And Satan will say when the matter has been decided: "Indeed, Allah promised you the promise of truth, and I promised you, but I failed you...﴾ up to His saying: ﴿Indeed, I disbelieve in your associating me [with Allah] before﴾ [Ibrahim: 22]. So he acknowledged that they had associated him with Allah before, that is, in the worldly life, and he did not disbelieve in their association until the Day of Resurrection.

The Prophet (ﷺ) clarified this meaning which we have explained in a hadith when 'Adi ibn Hatim (may Allah be pleased with him) asked him about His saying: ﴿They took their rabbis and their monks as lords besides Allah﴾ [al-Tawbah: 31], "How did they take them as lords?" He (ﷺ) answered that they made lawful for them what Allah had forbidden, and forbade for them what Allah had made lawful, so they followed them, and by that following they took them as lords.

Among the clearest proofs for this is that when the disbelievers make lawful something that they know Allah has forbidden, or forbid something that they know Allah has made lawful, they increase in a new disbelief along with their first disbelief. This is in His saying: ﴿The postponement is only an increase in disbelief...﴾ up to His saying: ﴿And Allah does not guide the disbelieving people﴾ [al-Tawbah: 37].

In any case, there is no doubt that whoever obeys other than Allah in a legislation that opposes what Allah has legislated has associated that other with Allah, as His saying indicates: ﴿And likewise their partners have made attractive to many of the polytheists the killing of their children﴾ [al-An'am: 137]. He called them "partners" because they obeyed them in killing their children.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Or do they have partners who have legislated for them in religion that for which Allah has not permitted?﴾ [al-Shura: 21]. He, exalted is He, called those who legislate in religion what Allah has not permitted "partners." What further clarifies this is what Allah mentioned about Satan on the Day of Resurrection, that he says to those who associated him with Allah in the worldly life: ﴿Indeed, I disbelieve in your associating me [with Allah] before﴾. That association mentioned has nothing more to it than that he invited them to his obedience and they responded to him. This he explicitly stated in His saying concerning him: ﴿And I had no authority over you except that I invited you and you responded to me﴾, and the verse continues. This is clear, as you see.

**Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on Surah 42, verse 11:**

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Originator of the heavens and the earth. He has made for you mates from among yourselves, and of the cattle, mates. He multiplies you thereby.﴾

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Originator of the heavens and the earth﴾: its explanation has already been given at the beginning of the Surah "Fatir" (Originator).

His saying ﴿He has made for you mates from among yourselves﴾ means: He created for you mates from among yourselves. As we have already discussed in the Surah "al-Nahl" (The Bee), in the commentary on His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And Allah has made for you mates from among yourselves, and made for you, from your mates, sons and grandchildren﴾ [an-Nahl: 72]. We explained there that the intended meaning of "mates" (azwaj) is the females, as His saying clarifies: ﴿And among His signs is that He created for you mates from among yourselves, that you may find tranquillity in them, and He placed between you affection and mercy﴾ [ar-Rum: 21], and so on. Also His saying: ﴿And that He created the pair, the male and the female, from a drop when it is emitted﴾ [an-Najm: 45–46]. And His saying: ﴿Then He made of it the pair, the male and the female﴾ [al-Qiyamah: 39]. And His saying: ﴿By the night when it covers, and by the day when it appears, and by Him who created the male and the female﴾ [al-Layl: 1–3]. And His saying concerning Adam: ﴿O mankind, fear your Lord, who created you from one soul and created from it its mate﴾ [an-Nisa: 1]. And His saying also in the same regard: ﴿It is He who created you from one soul and made from it its mate, that he might find tranquillity in her﴾ [al-A'raf: 189]. And His saying also in the same regard: ﴿He created you from one soul, then made from it its mate﴾ [az-Zumar: 6].

His saying ﴿and of the cattle, mates﴾ refers to the eight kinds mentioned in His saying: ﴿eight mates: of the sheep two﴾ [al-An'am: 143], and in His saying: ﴿He created you from one soul, then made from it its mate, and sent down for you of the cattle eight mates﴾ [az-Zumar: 6]. They are the males and females of the sheep, the goats, the camels and the cattle, as we have already clarified in the Surah "Al 'Imran," in the commentary on His saying: ﴿and the cattle and the tilled land﴾ [Al 'Imran: 14].

(p-58) As for His saying in this noble verse: ﴿He multiplies you thereby﴾, the apparent meaning is that the pronoun of address in His saying "yadhra'ukum" (He multiplies you) includes both human beings and cattle. The predominance of human beings over cattle in the pronoun of the addressees in His saying ﴿yadhra'ukum﴾ is clear and presents no difficulty.

The verified view, if Allah wills, is that the pronoun in His saying "fihi" (thereby) refers to what was mentioned of males and females, both of the children of Adam and of the cattle, in His saying: ﴿He has made for you mates from among yourselves, and of the cattle, mates﴾. This holds whether we say the meaning is that He made for the children of Adam females from their own kind, that is, from their species, and made for the cattle females likewise, or we say that the intended meaning of "mates" is the males and females of both together.

If that is so, the meaning of the noble verse ﴿He multiplies you﴾, that is, He creates you, scatters you and spreads you, ﴿thereby﴾, that is, through what was mentioned of males and females, that is, within it, by way of reproduction, as is well known.

This is clarified by His saying: ﴿Fear your Lord, who created you from one soul and created from it its mate, and scattered from the two of them many men and women﴾ [an-Nisa: 1]. His saying ﴿and scattered from the two of them many men and women﴾ clarifies the meaning of His saying ﴿He multiplies you thereby﴾.

If it is said: what is the reason for the singular form of the pronoun in the prepositional phrase in His saying ﴿He multiplies you thereby﴾, although, according to what you have said, it refers to the males and females of human beings and cattle?

The answer: among the styles of the Arabic language in which the Qur'an was revealed is that a pronoun or demonstrative in the singular may refer back to a dual or plural, on account of what has been mentioned, for example.

An example of this in the pronoun is His saying: ﴿Say: Have you considered, if Allah took away your hearing and your sight and sealed over your hearts, what god other than Allah could restore them to you?﴾ [al-An'am: 46]. The pronoun in His saying "bihi" (them/it) is singular, although it refers back to the hearing, the sight and the hearts.

So His saying "yatikum bihi" means: bring it to you, that is, what was mentioned of your hearing, your sight and your hearts. From this meaning is the saying of Ru'bah ibn al-'Ajjaj:

*In them are lines of black and white,*
*as if on the skin there were the patterns of leprosy.*

So His saying "ka'anna" (as if) refers to what was mentioned: lines of black and white.

(p-59) An example of this in the demonstrative is His saying: ﴿neither old nor virgin, but between that﴾ [al-Baqarah: 68], that is, between that which was mentioned, old and virgin. And the saying of 'Abd Allah ibn al-Zib'ara al-Sahmi:

*Indeed for good and for evil there is a limit,*
*and both of those are a face and a side.*

That is, both of those which were mentioned: the good and the evil.

As for the view of whoever says that the pronoun in His saying "fihi" refers to the womb, and the view of whoever says it refers to the belly, and whoever says it refers to the act of making (ja'l) understood from "ja'ala" (He made), and the view of whoever says it refers to the arrangement (tadbir), and other views of this kind, they are contrary to what is correct.

The verified view, if Allah wills, is what we have mentioned, and knowledge is with Allah, Exalted is He.

* *

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿There is nothing like unto Him, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing﴾.

We have already given the discussion of this in the Surah "al-A'raf" in the commentary on His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿then He established Himself upon the Throne﴾ [al-A'raf: 54].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 42, verse 12:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿To Him belong the keys of the heavens and the earth. He extends provision for whom He wills and restricts it.﴾

The "maqalid" of the heavens and the earth are their keys (mafatih). It is a plural with no singular from its own root: its singular is iqlid, and its plural maqalid is irregular (ala ghayr qiyas). Iqlid means "key" (miftah). It has also been said that its singular is miqlid, but this opinion is not well known in the language.

His, exalted and majestic is He, being the possessor of the keys of the heavens and the earth, meaning their keys, is a metonymy (kinaya) for His, exalted and majestic is He, being alone the owner of the treasuries of the heavens and the earth, because ownership of their keys necessarily entails ownership of them.

Exalted and majestic is He has mentioned something similar in surah al-Zumar in His saying: ﴿Allah is the Creator of all things, and He is Guardian over all things. To Him belong the keys of the heavens and the earth…﴾ [al-Zumar: 62-63], to the end of the verse.

What this verse of al-Shura and the two verses of al-Zumar mentioned indicate, namely that He, exalted and majestic is He, is the owner of the treasuries of the heavens and the earth, has been made clear in other verses, such as His saying: ﴿And to Allah belong the treasuries of the heavens and the earth, but the hypocrites do not understand﴾ [al-Munafiqun: 7], and His saying: ﴿And there is not a thing but that with Us are its treasuries, and We send it down only in a known measure﴾ [al-Hijr: 21].

(p-60) He has also made clear in other places that the treasuries of His mercy cannot belong to anyone else, such as:

• His saying: ﴿Or do they have the treasuries of the mercy of your Lord, the Mighty, the Bestower?﴾ [Sad: 9].

• His saying: ﴿Or do they have the treasuries of your Lord, or are they the controllers?﴾ [al-Tur: 37].

• His saying: ﴿Say: If you possessed the treasuries of the mercy of my Lord, you would then withhold them, for fear of spending; and man is ever tight-fisted﴾ [al-Isra': 100].

His saying in this noble verse: ﴿He extends provision for whom He wills and restricts it﴾ has its meaning made clear in other verses, such as:

• His saying: ﴿Say: Indeed my Lord extends provision for whom He wills of His servants and restricts it for him﴾ [Saba': 39], to the end of the verse.

• His saying: ﴿Say: Indeed my Lord extends provision for whom He wills and restricts it, but most people do not know﴾ [Saba': 36].

• His saying: ﴿Allah extends provision for whom He wills and restricts it, and they rejoice in the worldly life﴾ [al-Ra'd: 26], to the end of the verse.

• His saying: ﴿And Allah has favoured some of you over others in provision﴾ [al-Nahl: 71], to the end of the verse.

• His saying: ﴿We have apportioned among them their livelihood in the worldly life﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 32], to the end of the verse.

• His saying: ﴿If he be rich or poor, Allah is more entitled to both of them﴾ [al-Nisa': 135], to the end of the verse.

• His saying: ﴿Let the one of wealth spend from his wealth, and whoever has his provision restricted, let him spend from what Allah has given him﴾ [al-Talaq: 7], to the end of the verse. And His saying: ﴿And whoever has his provision restricted﴾ [al-Talaq: 7].

That is, his provision is constricted for him because of its scarcity. Likewise His saying: ﴿He extends provision for whom He wills and restricts it﴾ in the verses mentioned.

That is: He extends provision for whomever He wills to extend it to, and He restricts it, that is, He constricts provision for whomever He wills to constrict it upon, as we have explained in surah al-Anbiya' in the discussion of His saying: ﴿So he thought that We would not decree upon him﴾ [al-Anbiya': 87].

In some verses, exalted and majestic is He, has also made clear the wisdom of His constricting provision for whomever He constricts it upon.

He mentioned that among the ruling of this is that the extension of provision to a person may lead him to rebellion and tyranny, as in His saying: ﴿And if Allah were to extend provision to His servants, they would surely commit excess in the earth; but He sends down in measure what He wills. Indeed He is Acquainted and Seeing of His servants﴾ [al-Shura: 27], and His saying: ﴿Nay! Indeed, man does transgress, when he sees himself self-sufficient﴾ [al-Alaq: 6-7].

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿شَرَعَ لَكم مِنَ الدِّينِ ما وصّى بِهِ نُوحًا والَّذِي أوْحَيْنا إلَيْكَ وما وصَّيْنا بِهِ إبْراهِيمَ ومُوسى وعِيسى أنْ أقِيمُوا الدِّينَ﴾.

قَدْ قَدَّمْنا الكَلامَ عَلَيْهِ في سُورَةِ "الأحزابِ" في الكَلامِ عَلى قَوْلِهِ تَعالى: (p-61) ﴿وَإذْ أخَذْنا مِنَ النَّبِيِّينَ مِيثاقَهم ومِنكَ ومِن نُوحٍ﴾ الآيَةَ [الأحزاب: 7].

* *

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿وَلا تَتَفَرَّقُوا فِيهِ﴾.

الضَّمِيرُ في قَوْلِهِ: (فِيهِ) راجِعٌ إلى الدِّينِ في قَوْلِهِ: ﴿أنْ أقِيمُوا الدِّينَ﴾.

وما تَضَمَّنَتْهُ هَذِهِ الآيَةُ الكَرِيمَةُ مِنَ النَّهْيِ عَنِ الِافْتِراقِ في الدِّينِ جاءَ مُبَيَّنًا في غَيْرِ هَذا المَوْضِعِ، وقَدْ بَيَّنَ تَعالى أنَّهُ وصّى خَلْقَهُ بِذَلِكَ. فَمِنَ الآياتِ الدّالَّةِ عَلى ذَلِكَ قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿واعْتَصِمُوا بِحَبْلِ اللَّهِ جَمِيعًا ولا تَفَرَّقُوا﴾ الآيَةَ [آل عمران: 103]. وقَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿وَأنَّ هَذا صِراطِي مُسْتَقِيمًا فاتَّبِعُوهُ ولا تَتَّبِعُوا السُّبُلَ فَتَفَرَّقَ بِكم عَنْ سَبِيلِهِ ذَلِكم وصّاكم بِهِ لَعَلَّكم تَتَّقُونَ﴾ [الأنعام: 153].

وقَدْ بَيَّنَ تَعالى في بَعْضِ المَواضِعِ أنَّ بَعْضَ النّاسِ لا يَجْتَنِبُونَ هَذا النَّهْيَ، وهَدَّدَهُمْ عَلى ذَلِكَ، كَقَوْلِهِ تَعالى: ﴿إنَّ الَّذِينَ فَرَّقُوا دِينَهم وكانُوا شِيَعًا لَسْتَ مِنهم في شَيْءٍ إنَّما أمْرُهم إلى اللَّهِ ثُمَّ يُنَبِّئُهم بِما كانُوا يَفْعَلُونَ﴾ [الأنعام: 159]. لِأنَّ قَوْلَهُ: ﴿لَسْتَ مِنهم في شَيْءٍ﴾ إلى قَوْلِهِ: ﴿يَفْعَلُونَ﴾ فِيهِ تَهْدِيدٌ عَظِيمٌ لَهم.

وقَوْلُهُ تَعالى في سُورَةِ "قَدْ أفْلَحَ المُؤْمِنُونَ": ﴿وَإنَّ هَذِهِ أُمَّتُكم أُمَّةً واحِدَةً وأنا رَبُّكم فاتَّقُونِ﴾ ﴿فَتَقَطَّعُوا أمْرَهم بَيْنَهم زُبُرًا كُلُّ حِزْبٍ بِما لَدَيْهِمْ فَرِحُونَ﴾ ﴿فَذَرْهم في غَمْرَتِهِمْ حَتّى حِينٍ﴾ [المؤمنون: 52-54].

فَقَوْلُهُ: ﴿وَإنَّ هَذِهِ أُمَّتُكم أُمَّةً واحِدَةً﴾ أيْ: إنَّ هَذِهِ شَرِيعَتُكم شَرِيعَةٌ واحِدَةٌ، ودِينُكم دِينٌ واحِدٌ، ورَبُّكم واحِدٌ، فَلا تَتَفَرَّقُوا في الدِّينِ.

وقَوْلُهُ - جَلَّ وعَلا -: ﴿فَتَقَطَّعُوا أمْرَهم بَيْنَهم زُبُرًا﴾ دَلِيلٌ عَلى أنَّهم لَمْ يَجْتَنِبُوا ما نُهُوا عَنْهُ مِن ذَلِكَ.

وقَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿فَذَرْهم في غَمْرَتِهِمْ حَتّى حِينٍ﴾ فِيهِ تَهْدِيدٌ لَهم ووَعِيدٌ عَظِيمٌ عَلى ذَلِكَ. ونَظِيرُ ذَلِكَ قَوْلُهُ تَعالى في سُورَةِ "الأنْبِياءِ": ﴿إنَّ هَذِهِ أُمَّتُكم أُمَّةً واحِدَةً وأنا رَبُّكم فاعْبُدُونِ﴾ ﴿وَتَقَطَّعُوا أمْرَهم بَيْنَهم كُلٌّ إلَيْنا راجِعُونَ﴾ [الأنبياء: 92-93]. فَقَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿كُلٌّ إلَيْنا راجِعُونَ﴾ فِيهِ أيْضًا تَهْدِيدٌ لَهم ووَعِيدٌ عَلى ذَلِكَ، وقَدْ أوْضَحْنا تَفْسِيرَ هَذِهِ الآياتِ في آخِرِ سُورَةِ "الأنْبِياءِ" في الكَلامِ عَلى قَوْلِهِ تَعالى: ﴿إنَّ هَذِهِ أُمَّتُكم أُمَّةً واحِدَةً﴾ الآيَةَ [الأنبياء: 93].

(p-62) وقَدْ جاءَ في الحَدِيثِ المَشْهُورِ افْتِراقُ اليَهُودِ عَلى إحْدى وسَبْعِينَ فِرْقَةً، وافْتِراقُ النَّصارى إلى اثْنَتَيْنِ وسَبْعِينَ فِرْقَةً، وافْتِراقُ هَذِهِ الأُمَّةِ إلى ثَلاثٍ وسَبْعِينَ فِرْقَةً، وأنَّ النّاجِيَةَ مِنها واحِدَةٌ، وهي الَّتِي كانَتْ عَلى ما كانَ عَلَيْهِ النَّبِيُّ (ﷺ) وأصْحابُهُ.

* *

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿كَبُرَ عَلى المُشْرِكِينَ ما تَدْعُوهم إلَيْهِ﴾.

بَيَّنَ - جَلَّ وعَلا - أنَّهُ ﴿كَبُرَ عَلى المُشْرِكِينَ﴾ أيْ شَقَّ عَلَيْهِمْ وعَظُمَ ما يَدْعُوهم إلَيْهِ (ﷺ) مِن عِبادَةِ اللَّهِ تَعالى وحْدَهُ، وطاعَتِهِ بِامْتِثالِ أمْرِهِ واجْتِنابِ نَهْيِهِ. ولِعِظَمِ ذَلِكَ ومَشَقَّتِهِ عَلَيْهِمْ كانُوا يَكْرَهُونَ ما أنْزَلَ اللَّهُ، ويَجْتَهِدُونَ في عَدَمِ سَماعِهِ لِشِدَّةِ كَراهَتِهِمْ لَهُ، بَلْ يَكادُونَ يَبْطِشُونَ بِمَن يَتْلُو عَلَيْهِمْ آياتِ رَبِّهِمْ لِشِدَّةِ بُغْضِهِمْ وكَراهَتِهِمْ لَها.

والآياتُ المُوَضِّحَةُ لِهَذا المَعْنى كَثِيرَةٌ في كِتابِ اللَّهِ، وفِيها بَيانُ أنَّ ذَلِكَ هو عادَةُ الكافِرِينَ مَعَ جَمِيعِ الرُّسُلِ مِن عَهْدِ نُوحٍ إلى عَهْدِ مُحَمَّدٍ (ﷺ).

فَقَدْ بَيَّنَ تَعالى مَشَقَّةَ ذَلِكَ عَلى قَوْمِ نُوحٍ وكِبْرَهُ عَلَيْهِمْ في مَواضِعَ مِن كِتابِهِ، كَقَوْلِهِ تَعالى: ﴿واتْلُ عَلَيْهِمْ نَبَأ نُوحٍ إذْ قالَ لِقَوْمِهِ ياقَوْمِ إنْ كانَ كَبُرَ عَلَيْكم مَقامِي وتَذْكِيرِي بِآياتِ اللَّهِ فَعَلى اللَّهِ تَوَكَّلْتُ﴾ الآيَةَ [يونس: 71]. وقَوْلِهِ تَعالى عَنْ نُوحٍ: ﴿وَإنِّي كُلَّما دَعَوْتُهم لِتَغْفِرَ لَهم جَعَلُوا أصابِعَهم في آذانِهِمْ واسْتَغْشَوْا ثِيابَهم وأصَرُّوا واسْتَكْبَرُوا اسْتِكْبارًا﴾ [نوح: 7].

فَقَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿جَعَلُوا أصابِعَهم في آذانِهِمْ واسْتَغْشَوْا ثِيابَهُمْ﴾ يَدُلُّ دَلالَةً واضِحَةً عَلى شِدَّةِ بُغْضِهِمْ وكَراهَتِهِمْ لِما يَدْعُوهم إلَيْهِ نُوحٌ، فَهو واضِحٌ في أنَّهم كَبُرَ عَلَيْهِمْ ما يَدْعُوهم إلَيْهِ مِن تَوْحِيدِ اللَّهِ والإيمانِ بِهِ.

وقَدْ بَيَّنَ اللَّهُ تَعالى مِثْلَ ذَلِكَ في الكُفّارِ الَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا نَبِيَّنا مُحَمَّدًا (ﷺ) في آياتٍ مِن كِتابِهِ، كَقَوْلِهِ تَعالى: ﴿وَإذا تُتْلى عَلَيْهِمْ آياتُنا بَيِّناتٍ تَعْرِفُ في وُجُوهِ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا المُنْكَرَ يَكادُونَ يَسْطُونَ بِالَّذِينَ يَتْلُونَ عَلَيْهِمْ آياتِنا﴾ [الحج: 72]. فَقَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿تَعْرِفُ في وُجُوهِ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا المُنْكَرَ﴾ الآيَةَ، يَدُلُّ دَلالَةً واضِحَةً عَلى شِدَّةِ بُغْضِهِمْ وكَراهِيَتِهِمْ لِسَماعِ تِلْكَ الآياتِ.

وَ

• كَقَوْلِهِ تَعالى: ﴿وَقالَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لا تَسْمَعُوا لِهَذا القُرْآنِ والغَوْا فِيهِ﴾ الآيَةَ [فصلت: 26].

• وقَوْلِهِ تَعالى في "الزُّخْرُفِ": ﴿لَقَدْ جِئْناكم بِالحَقِّ ولَكِنَّ أكْثَرَكم لِلْحَقِّ كارِهُونَ﴾ [الزخرف: 78]. (p-63)

• وَقَوْلِهِ تَعالى في "قَدْ أفْلَحَ المُؤْمِنُونَ": ﴿أمْ يَقُولُونَ بِهِ جِنَّةٌ بَلْ جاءَهم بِالحَقِّ وأكْثَرُهم لِلْحَقِّ كارِهُونَ﴾ [المؤمنون: 70].

• وقَوْلِهِ تَعالى في "القِتالِ": ﴿ذَلِكَ بِأنَّهم كَرِهُوا ما أنْزَلَ اللَّهُ فَأحْبَطَ أعْمالَهُمْ﴾ [محمد: 9].

• وقَوْلِهِ تَعالى: ﴿تِلْكَ آياتُ اللَّهِ نَتْلُوها عَلَيْكَ بِالحَقِّ فَبِأيِّ حَدِيثٍ بَعْدَ اللَّهِ وآياتِهِ يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ ﴿وَيْلٌ لِكُلِّ أفّاكٍ أثِيمٍ﴾ ﴿يَسْمَعُ آياتِ اللَّهِ تُتْلى عَلَيْهِ ثُمَّ يُصِرُّ مُسْتَكْبِرًا كَأنْ لَمْ يَسْمَعْها فَبَشِّرْهُ بِعَذابٍ ألِيمٍ﴾ [الجاثية: 6-8].

• وقَوْلِهِ تَعالى: ﴿وَإذا تُتْلى عَلَيْهِ آياتُنا ولّى مُسْتَكْبِرًا كَأنْ لَمْ يَسْمَعْها كَأنَّ في أُذُنَيْهِ وقْرًا فَبَشِّرْهُ بِعَذابٍ ألِيمٍ﴾ [لقمان: 7].

• وقَوْلِهِ تَعالى: ﴿وَقالُوا قُلُوبُنا في أكِنَّةٍ مِمّا تَدْعُونا إلَيْهِ وفي آذانِنا وقْرٌ ومِن بَيْنِنا وبَيْنِكَ حِجابٌ﴾ الآيَةَ [فصلت: 5].

والآياتُ بِمِثْلِ ذَلِكَ كَثِيرَةٌ.

واعْلَمْ أنَّ هَؤُلاءِ الَّذِينَ يَكْرَهُونَ ما أنْزَلَ اللَّهُ يَجِبُ عَلى كُلِّ مُسْلِمٍ أنْ يَحْذَرَ كُلَّ الحَذَرِ مِن أنْ يُطِيعَهم في بَعْضِ أمْرِهِمْ؛ لِأنَّ ذَلِكَ يَسْتَلْزِمُ نَتائِجَ سَيِّئَةً مُتَناهِيَةً في السُّوءِ، كَما أوْضَحَ تَعالى ذَلِكَ في قَوْلِهِ: ﴿أفَلا يَتَدَبَّرُونَ القُرْآنَ أمْ عَلى قُلُوبٍ أقْفالُها﴾ ﴿إنَّ الَّذِينَ ارْتَدُّوا عَلى أدْبارِهِمْ مِن بَعْدِ ما تَبَيَّنَ لَهُمُ الهُدى الشَّيْطانُ سَوَّلَ لَهم وأمْلى لَهُمْ﴾ ﴿ذَلِكَ بِأنَّهم قالُوا لِلَّذِينَ كَرِهُوا ما نَزَّلَ اللَّهُ سَنُطِيعُكم في بَعْضِ الأمْرِ واللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ إسْرارَهُمْ﴾ ﴿فَكَيْفَ إذا تَوَفَّتْهُمُ المَلائِكَةُ يَضْرِبُونَ وُجُوهَهم وأدْبارَهُمْ﴾ ﴿ذَلِكَ بِأنَّهُمُ اتَّبَعُوا ما أسْخَطَ اللَّهَ وكَرِهُوا رِضْوانَهُ فَأحْبَطَ أعْمالَهُمْ﴾ [محمد: 24-28]. فَعَلى كُلِّ مُسْلِمٍ أنْ يَحْذَرَ ثُمَّ يَحْذَرَ ثُمَّ يَحْذَرَ كُلَّ الحَذَرِ مِن أنْ يَقُولَ لِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا، الَّذِينَ يَكْرَهُونَ ما أنْزَلَ اللَّهُ: سَنُطِيعُكم في بَعْضِ الأمْرِ؛ لِأنَّ ذَلِكَ يُسَبِّبُ لَهُ ما ذَكَرَهُ اللَّهُ في الآياتِ المَذْكُورَةِ، ويَكْفِيهِ زَجْرًا ورَدْعًا عَنْ ذَلِكَ قَوْلُ رَبِّهِ تَعالى: ﴿فَكَيْفَ إذا تَوَفَّتْهُمُ المَلائِكَةُ يَضْرِبُونَ وُجُوهَهم وأدْبارَهُمْ﴾ إلى قَوْلِهِ ﴿فَأحْبَطَ أعْمالَهُمْ﴾ [محمد: 27-28].

* *

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿اللَّهُ يَجْتَبِي إلَيْهِ مَن يَشاءُ ويَهْدِي إلَيْهِ مَن يُنِيبُ﴾.

الِاجْتِباءُ (ismtiba': choosing and selecting) في اللُّغَةِ العَرَبِيَّةِ مَعْناهُ الِاخْتِيارُ والِاصْطِفاءُ.

وقَدْ دَلَّتْ هَذِهِ الآيَةُ الكَرِيمَةُ عَلى أنَّهُ تَعالى يَجْتَبِي مِن خَلْقِهِ مَن يَشاءُ اجْتِباءَهُ.

وقَدْ بَيَّنَ في مَواضِعَ أُخَرَ بَعْضَ مَن شاءَ اجْتِباءَهُ مِن خَلْقِهِ، فَبَيَّنَ أنَّ مِنهُمُ المُؤْمِنِينَ مِن هَذِهِ الأُمَّةِ في قَوْلِهِ تَعالى: ﴿ياأيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا ارْكَعُوا واسْجُدُوا واعْبُدُوا رَبَّكم وافْعَلُوا الخَيْرَ﴾ إلى قَوْلِهِ: ﴿هُوَ اجْتَباكم وما جَعَلَ عَلَيْكم في الدِّينِ مِن حَرَجٍ﴾ [الحج: 77-78].

(p-64) وقَوْلِهِ تَعالى: ﴿ثُمَّ أوْرَثْنا الكِتابَ الَّذِينَ اصْطَفَيْنا مِن عِبادِنا﴾ الآيَةَ [فاطر: 32].

وبَيَّنَ في مَوْضِعٍ آخَرَ أنَّ مِنهم آدَمَ، وهو قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿ثُمَّ اجْتَباهُ رَبُّهُ فَتابَ عَلَيْهِ وهَدى﴾ [طه: 122]. وذَكَرَ أنَّ مِنهم إبْراهِيمَ في قَوْلِهِ: ﴿إنَّ إبْراهِيمَ كانَ أُمَّةً﴾ إلى قَوْلِهِ ﴿شاكِرًا لِأنْعُمِهِ اجْتَباهُ﴾ الآيَةَ [النحل: 120-121]. إلى غَيْرِ ذَلِكَ مِنَ الآياتِ الدّالَّةِ عَلى اجْتِباءِ بَعْضِ الخَلْقِ بِالتَّعْيِينِ.

وقَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿وَيَهْدِي إلَيْهِ مَن يُنِيبُ﴾ أيْ مَن سَبَقَ في عِلْمِهِ أنَّهُ يُنِيبُ إلى اللَّهِ، أيْ يَرْجِعُ إلى ما يُرْضِيهِ مِنَ الإيمانِ والطّاعَةِ. ونَظِيرُ هَذِهِ الآيَةِ قَوْلُهُ تَعالى في سُورَةِ "الرَّعْدِ": ﴿قُلْ إنَّ اللَّهَ يُضِلُّ مَن يَشاءُ ويَهْدِي إلَيْهِ مَن أنابَ﴾ [الرعد: 27].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 42, verse 15:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And say: "I believe in whatever Book Allah has sent down, and I have been commanded to act justly between you."﴾

The verses clarifying this were given earlier in Surah al-Baqarah, in the discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And what was given to the prophets from their Lord—we make no distinction between any one of them﴾ [al-Baqarah: 136].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 42, verse 17:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿It is Allah who has sent down the Book with truth, and the Balance.﴾

In this noble verse, He—majestic and exalted—makes clear that He is the One who sent down the Book in a state of being clothed with the truth, which is the opposite of falsehood. His saying "the Book" (al-Kitab) is a noun of genus (ism jins), intended to refer to all the heavenly scriptures.

We have already explained in surah al-Hajj that the singular form which is a noun of genus may be used with the intention of the plural, and we mentioned the verses indicating this together with the Arabic evidence.

His saying, may He be exalted, in this noble verse: "and the Balance" means that Allah—majestic and exalted—is the One who sent down the Balance, and what is intended by it is justice and equity.

Some scholars said: the Balance in the verse is the well-known instrument of weighing.

What supports this is that al-mizan (al-Mizan) is on the pattern mif‘al (mif‘al), and the pattern mif‘al is analogical for the name of an instrument.

According to the first interpretation—namely that the Balance is justice and equity—the well-known instrument of weighing is included in it, because establishing weighing with fairness is part of justice and equity.

What this noble verse includes, that Allah, may He be exalted, is the One who sent down the Book and the Balance, He has clarified in other places, such as His saying in surah al-Hadid: ﴿We certainly sent Our messengers with clear proofs, and sent down with them the Book and the Balance so that people may uphold justice.﴾ [al-Hadid: 25]

So He stated explicitly that He sent down with His messengers the Book and the Balance so that people would establish justice with fairness, which is justice and equity. And as His saying in surah al-Rahman: ﴿And the sky—He raised it and set up the balance. That you not transgress within the balance. And establish weight with justice and do not make the balance deficient.﴾ [al-Rahman: 7–9]

The author of this commentary—may Allah pardon him and forgive him—says: What appears to me, and Allah the Exalted knows best, is that the Balance in surah al-Shura and surah al-Hadid is justice and equity, as many commentators have said.

And that the Balance in surah al-Rahman is the well-known balance, I mean the instrument by which some goods are weighed.

What indicates this is that in surah al-Shura and surah al-Hadid He used the expression "sending down" the Balance, not "setting it up," and He said in surah al-Shura: ﴿It is Allah who has sent down the Book with truth and the Balance.﴾ And in al-Hadid: ﴿And We sent down with them the Book and the Balance.﴾ [al-Hadid: 25]

As for surah al-Rahman, He used the expression "setting up" and not "sending down," saying: ﴿And the sky—He raised it and set up the balance.﴾ [al-Rahman: 7] Then He followed this with what indicates that what is intended is the well-known instrument of weighing, and that is in His saying: ﴿And establish weight with justice and do not make the balance deficient.﴾ [al-Rahman: 9] Because the Balance which they were forbidden to make deficient is the brother of the measure (al-mikyal), as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Give full measure and do not be among the losers. And weigh with an even balance. And do not deprive people of their things.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 181–183] And He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Woe to the defrauders, who, when they take a measure from people, take it in full, and when they measure or weigh for them, they give less.﴾ [al-Mutaffifin: 1–3] And He, the Exalted, said about His prophet Shu'ayb: ﴿And do not diminish the measure and the balance﴾ [Hud: 84], the verse. And He, the Exalted, also said about him: ﴿There has certainly come to you clear evidence from your Lord, so give full measure and balance﴾ [al-A'raf: 85], the verse. And He, the Exalted, said in surah al-An'am: ﴿And give full measure and balance with justice; We do not charge a soul except [with] its capacity﴾ [al-An'am: 152]. And He, the Exalted, said in surah Bani Isra'il: ﴿And give full measure when you measure and weigh with an even balance. That is better and best in result﴾ [al-Isra': 35].

If it is said: You have chosen that what is intended by the Balance in surah al-Shura and surah al-Hadid is justice and equity, and that what is intended by the Balance in surah al-Rahman is the well-known instrument of weighing, and you have mentioned similar verses of the Qur'an.
